Dominant Chord Extentions · Level 1.heading: Hear the dominant chord. Find the added notes.
Dominant Chord Extentions · Level 1.intro: Dominant 7 is already given. Listen and select all the extra extensions you hear above that chord.

steps.title: Listen to the whole chord
steps.description: Press Play and listen to how the extra notes change the dominant seventh chord. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Select all the added extensions
steps.description: Choose all the extensions present, such as ♭9 and ♯11, or 9 and 13. More than one answer is needed. Tap a selected extension again to remove it.

steps.title: Check and submit
steps.description: Check every selected extension, then press Submit Answer. The seventh is already part of the given Dominant 7 chord, so there is no separate 7 button to choose.

Dominant Chord Extentions · Level 1.about: A dominant seventh chord already contains four notes. In F, they are F, A, C and E♭. This quiz asks which extra notes are added to that chord. The ♭ sign means a lowered note and ♯ means a raised note, by one keyboard step, counting white and black keys. Group 1 contains seven chords with a lowered ninth (♭9), a raised ninth (♯9), or both. This lesson uses chords built on F. The chords use their basic arrangement, with no doubled or shifted notes. Select every extension present. For example, a chord with both ♭9 and ♯9 needs both buttons selected.
Dominant Chord Extentions · Level 1.exampleExplanation: F, A, C and E♭ make the dominant seventh chord. G♭ adds ♭9 and B adds ♯11, so select ♭9 and ♯11.
